Subject: Staging cutover: large packet uploads failing (SYN retransmits)

Hi Vivek,

We're cutting over the staging site to the new private connector tonight and we've run into an issue: large uploads (~5MB) to our on-prem S3 proxy are failing — TCP shows repeated SYN retransmits from customer side and the connection never establishes. Small uploads succeed.

Attached a condensed pcap and tcpdump. We also ran traceroutes and saw inconsistent MTU along the path; our ASA shows "fragment reassembly failed" messages.

Can you triage with your private-deploy team? This is blocking the cutover and we'd like a remediation plan before our maintenance window tomorrow evening.

Attachments: acme_staging_pcap.zip (pcap)

Thanks,
Sam

Subject: Re: Staging cutover: large packet uploads failing (SYN retransmits)

Vivek / Sam —

I pulled the pcap (thanks), reproducing notes below and a short mitigation plan. High-level: signs point to an MTU/fragmentation path issue + NAT behavior that drops larger MSS during handshake.

What I see:
- SYN from staging with MSS ~1460, path returns SYN-ACK with no options sometimes; retransmits correlated with DF-set packets.
- ASA logs show "fragment reassembly failed" and occasional ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages that are not getting back to the sender (ICMP filtered).
- On our gateway the conntrack entries are getting created but some flows are reset when fragments arrive out-of-order.

Immediate mitigation to test (non-invasive):
1) On your ASA (or a test host) clamp MSS on outbound clients to 1360: e.g., on Linux hosts iptables:
   iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360
2) On our private gateway (staging) temporarily disable tcp segmentation offload on the NIC and set net.ipv4.tcp_moderate_rcvbuf=0 to avoid kernel coalescing artifacts.
3) If fragments are being dropped by the firewall, confirm we can allow ICMP type 3/code 4 (fragmentation needed) back to the origin — otherwise PMTU cannot converge.

If MSS clamp works we can push the setting as a short-lived policy for the cutover. I've dropped a short test plan and example config in the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example (mss-test-plan.md). Attachment: mss-test-plan.md

Commands I would run (staging gateway):
- ethtool -K eth0 tx off rx off gso off gro off
- sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_moderate_rcvbuf=0
- iptables -t raw -A PREROUTING -p tcp -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j CT --helper ftp

Note on NAT: if there is a symmetric SNAT on the ASA that rewrites ports inconsistently for fragments, reassembly may fail; please provide a short ASA config snippet if possible (edge-config-snippet.txt).

I can be on the 20:00 UTC window. If you want, we can do a smaller canary at 18:30 UTC to verify test uploads.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Network Lead, Private Deployments

Thanks Karthik — makes sense. A few replies/questions: 

- ASA MTU is 1500 (no jumbo frames). The on-prem storage array switch is at 9000 but the ASA fronting it is 1500.
- We do have an inspection policy on the ASA that touches TCP (some ALG-like behavior) and it does NAT. I can pull the minimal config and attach (will add edge-config-snippet.txt).
- Our firewall team confirmed they drop fragments by default and we currently block ICMP type 3/code 4 for historical "security" reasons. I will request a temporary exception for the window.

We can try the 18:30 UTC small canary and then the main window at 20:00 UTC. For the canary, what's the minimum test you need? We can coordinate a 50MB upload from a staging host and monitor the ASA logs.

Sam

Sam / team —

Thanks for confirming the ASA/switch discrepancy and for pulling the config. Plan below (canary + rollback):

Canary (2027-04-06 18:30 UTC):
- Redwood will apply temporary MSS clamp on staging-gateway (1360) and disable GSO/GRO on the test interface.
- Acme will allow ICMP type 3/code 4 for the test IPs and monitor ASA logs; perform a 50MB upload from a staging host to S3 proxy.
- Success criteria: upload completes within 60s and no SYN retransmit spikes; ASA logs show ICMP fragmentation-needed sent back.

Main cutover (20:00 UTC):
- If canary passes, we push MSS clamp rule at edge (either on ASA or on a pre-ingress filter) for duration of cutover window.
- Post-cutover (rollback): remove MSS clamp and re-enable GSO/GRO on gateway NICs; confirm uploads still succeed for sample traffic.

Contingencies:
- If MSS clamp fails to stabilize sessions, Redwood can provision a short-lived dedicated egress route from our dedicated pool to your proxy (no change to ASA) to validate path without modifying customer firewall — this is heavier and we prefer the clamp test first.

Point contacts: Vivek (private deploy lead) + Karthik (network lead) + Sam (Acme NetOps). I'll join the call at 18:15 UTC to coordinate.

Vivek
